<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">received in 2011.&#160; In addition, on February&nbsp;22, 2012, the FHLB announced the payment of a dividend to its member banks at an annualized rate of 0.10% based on the bank&#146;s average FHLB stock holding for the fourth quarter of 2011.&#160; On February&nbsp;23, 2012, the Bank received a dividend of $392 from the FHLB.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management evaluates restricted stock for impairment in accordance with the accounting standard relating to <i>Accounting by Certain Entities (Including Entities With Trade Receivables) That Lend to or Finance the Activities of Others</i>.&#160; Management&#146;s determination of whether these investments are impaired is based on its assessment of the ultimate recoverability of the cost rather than by recognizing temporary declines in value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management believes no impairment charge is necessary related to the restricted stock as of December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Transfers of Financial Assets</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Transfers of financial assets, including loans and loan participation sales, are accounted for as sales, when control over the assets has been surrendered.&#160; Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when (1)&nbsp;the assets have been isolated from the Corporation, (2)&nbsp;the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets and (3)&nbsp;the Corporation does not maintain effective control over the transferred assets through an agreement to repurchase them before their maturity.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Cash Value of Life Insurance</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation invests in bank owned life insurance (&#147;BOLI&#148;) as a source of funding employee benefit expenses.&#160; BOLI involves the purchase of life insurance by the Corporation on a chosen group of directors and select management of the Bank.&#160; The Corporation is the owner and beneficiary of the policies.&#160; The life insurance investment is carried at the cash surrender value of the underlying policies.&#160; These amounts are immediately available to the Corporation upon surrender of the policies.&#160; Income generated from the increase in the cash surrender value of the policies is included in other income on the income statement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Foreclosed Assets</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Real estate and other foreclosed assets acquired in settlement of loans are carried at fair value of the property less estimated cost to sell at the date of acquisition.&#160; Subsequent to acquisition, foreclosed assets are carried at the lower of cost or estimated fair value of the property less selling costs.&#160; Any write-down, at or prior to the dates the assets are foreclosed, is charged to the allowance for loan losses.&#160; Subsequent write-downs and expenses incurred in connection with holding such assets are reported in other expenses.&#160; Any gains or losses resulting from the sale of foreclosed assets are recorded in other income.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Goodwill</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill represents the excess of the cost of an acquisition over the fair value of the tangible and identifiable intangible assets acquired.&#160; As a result of the adoption of the accounting standard relating to <i>Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</i>, business acquisition goodwill is no longer</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">51<a name="PB_51_151839_563"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">amortized into the income statement over an estimated life, but rather is tested at least annually for impairment.&#160; Based upon the goodwill analysis performed by an independent third party, there was no goodwill impairment for the 2011 year end.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Intangible Assets</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Intangible assets represent purchased assets that lack physical substance but can be distinguished from goodwill because of contractual or other legal rights.&#160; The Corporation&#146;s intangible assets consist of a core deposit intangible, which has a finite life and is amortized over its estimated useful life.&#160; Mortgage servicing rights are also included in intangible assets where the Bank recognized a servicing fee at the time of the sale for the right to service mortgages and other loans sold.&#160; The servicing asset is amortized as an expense over the life of the loan for which the Bank retains the servicing rights.&#160; Intangible assets are also subject to impairment testing when an indication of impairment exists.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Federal Income Taxes</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The provision for income taxes is based on income as reported in the financial statements. Certain items of income and expense are recognized in different periods for financial reporting purposes than for federal income tax purposes.&#160; Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are determined using the liability (or balance sheet) method.&#160; Under this method, the net deferred tax asset or liability is determined based on the tax effects of the temporary differences between book and tax basis of the various balance sheet assets and liabilities given current recognition to changes in tax rates and laws.&#160; As changes in tax laws or rates are enacted, deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted through the provision for applicable income taxes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Treasury Stock</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Repurchases of common stock are recorded as treasury stock at cost.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Advertising</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Advertising costs are expensed as incurred and totaled $41,000 and $64,000 for the years ending December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Earnings Per Common Share</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic earnings per share represents income available to common stockholders divided by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the period.&#160; For diluted earnings per share, net income is divided by the weighted average number of shares outstanding plus the incremental number of shares added as a result of converting common stock equivalents.&#160; The Corporation&#146;s common stock equivalents consist of outstanding common stock options, which amounted to 170,000 options as of the 2011 and 2010 year ends.&#160; There was intrinsic value associated with the outstanding stock options at December&nbsp;31, 2011 because the exercise price for each of the options was lower than the trading price of the stock as compared with there being no intrinsic value at December&nbsp;31, 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Off Balance Sheet Financial Instruments</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the ordinary course of business, the Corporation has entered into off balance sheet financial instruments consisting of commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit.&#160; Such financial instruments are recorded in the financial statements when they become payable.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Segment Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation operates in a single business segment consisting of traditional banking activities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Comprehensive Income</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America require that recognized revenue, expenses, gains, and losses be included in net income.&#160; Changes in certain assets and liabilities, such as unrealized gains and losses on available-for-sale securities, are reported as a separate component of the equity section of the balance sheet.&#160; Such items, along with net income, are components of comprehensive income.&#160; Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss), which represents a component of shareholders&#146; equity, represents the net unrealized gain (loss) on securities available-for-sale, net of taxes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The components of other comprehensive income and related tax effects for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2011and 2010 are as follows:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Reclassifications</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For purposes of comparability, certain prior period amounts may have been reclassified to conform with the 2011 presentation.&#160; Such reclassifications had no impact on net income.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">New Accounting Standards</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2010, the FASB issued ASU 2010-06, <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures (Topic 820): Improving Disclosures about Fair Value Measurements</i>.&#160; ASU 2010-06 amends Subtopic 820-10 to clarify existing disclosures, require new disclosures, and includes conforming amendments to guidance on employers&#146; disclosures about postretirement benefit plan assets.&#160; ASU 2010-06 was effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2009, except for disclosures about purchases, sales, issuances, and settlements in the roll forward of activity in Level 3 fair value measurements.&#160; Those disclosures were effective for fiscal years beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2010 and for interim periods within those fiscal years.&#160; The adoption of the new guidance did not have a material impact on Riverview&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In July&nbsp;2010, the FASB issued ASU 2010-20, <i>Disclosures about the Credit Quality of Financing Receivables and the Allowance for Credit Losses</i>.&#160; The new disclosure guidance significantly expanded the existing requirements leading to greater transparency into a company&#146;s exposure to credit losses from lending arrangements.&#160; The extensive new disclosures of information as of the end of a reporting period was effective for annual reporting periods ending on or after December&nbsp;15, 2010 and has been presented in Note 4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.&#160; Specific disclosures regarding activity that occurred before the issuance of the ASU, such as the allowance roll forward and modification disclosures was required to be adopted for periods beginning on or after December&nbsp;15, 2010, and has also incorporated in Note 4.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2010, the FASB issued ASU 2010-28,&nbsp;Intangibles<i>&#151;Goodwill and Other (Topic 350), When to Perform Step 2 of the Goodwill Impairment Test for Reporting Units with Zero or Negative Carrying Amounts.</i>&#160; A</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SU 2010-28 affects all entities that have recognized goodwill and have one or more reporting units whose carrying amount for purposes of performing Step 1 of the goodwill impairment test is zero or negative.&#160; ASU 2010-28 modifies Step 1 so that for those reporting units, an entity is required to perform Step 2 of the goodwill impairment test if it is more likely than not that a goodwill impairment exists.&#160; In determining whether it is more likely than not that goodwill impairment exists, an entity should consider whether there are any adverse qualitative factors indicating that impairment may exist.&#160; The qualitative factors are consistent with existing guidance, which requires that goodwill of a reporting unit be tested for impairment between annual tests if an event occurs or circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying amount.&#160; This guidance was effective for Riverview for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2010.&#160; Adoption of ASU 2010-28 did not have a material impact on the Riverview&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-2, A <i>Creditor&#146;s Determination of Whether a Restructuring is a Troubled Debt Restructuring</i>.&#160; This guidance clarifies which loan modifications constitute troubled debt restructurings and is intended to assist creditors in determining whether a modification of the terms of a receivable meets the criteria to be considered a troubled debt restructuring, both for the purpose of recording an impairment charge and for disclosure of troubled debt restructurings.&#160; In evaluating whether a restructuring</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">54<a name="PB_54_151839_5250"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">constitutes a troubled debt restructuring, a creditor must separately conclude, under the guidance clarified by ASU 2011-2, that both of the following exist: (a) the restructuring constitutes a concession; and (b) the debtor is experiencing financial difficulties.&#160; As allowed by the guidance, Riverview adopted the provisions of ASU 2011-2 in the year ending December 31, 2011.&#160; See presentation of the disclosure in Note 4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April 2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-03, Transfers and Servicing (Topic 860) &#151; Reconsideration of Effective Control for Repurchase Agreements.&#160; The amendments in this ASU remove from the assessment of effective control (1) the criterion requiring the transferor to have the ability to repurchase or redeem the financial assets on substantially the agreed terms, even in the event of default by the transferee and (2) the collateral maintenance implementation guidance related to that criterion.&#160; The amendments in this ASU are effective for the first interim or annual period beginning on or after December 15, 2011.&#160; The guidance should be applied prospectively to transactions or modifications of existing transactions that occur on or after the effective date.&#160; Early adoption is not permitted.&#160; Riverview is currently assessing the impact that ASU 2011-03 will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May 2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-04, Fair Value Measurement (Topic 820) &#151; Amendments to Achieve Common Fair Value Measurement and Disclosure Requirements in U.S. GAAP and IFRSs.&#160; This ASU is the result of joint efforts by the FASB and IASB to develop a single, converged fair value framework on how (not when) to measure fair value and what disclosures to provide about fair value measurements.&#160; The ASU is largely consistent with existing fair value measurement principles in U.S. GAAP (Topic 820), with many of the amendments made to eliminate unnecessary wording differences between U.S. GAAP and IFRSs.&#160; The amendments are effective for public companies during the interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2011 with prospective application.&#160; For nonpublic entities, the amendments are effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2011.&#160; Early application is not permitted.&#160; Riverview is currently assessing the impact that ASU 2011-04 will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June 2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-05, Comprehensive Income (Topic 220) &#151; Presentation of Comprehensive Income.&#160; The objective of this ASU is to improve the comparability, consistency and transparency of financial reporting and to increase the prominence of items reported in other comprehensive income by eliminating the option to present components of other comprehensive income as part of the statement of changes in stockholders&#146; equity.&#160; The amendments require that all non-owner changes in stockholders&#146; equity be presented either in a single continuous statement of comprehensive income or in two separate but consecutive statements.&#160; The single statement of comprehensive income should include the components of net income, a total for net income, the components of other comprehensive income, a total for other comprehensive income, and a total for comprehensive income.&#160; In the two-statement approach, the first statement should present total net income and its components followed consecutively by a second statement that should present all the components of other comprehensive income, a total for other comprehensive income, and a total for comprehensive income.&#160; The amendments do not change the items that must be reported in other comprehensive income, the option for an entity to present components of other comprehensive income either net of related tax effects or before related tax effects, or the calculation or reporting of earnings per share.&#160; The amendments in this ASU should be applied retrospectively.&#160; For public companies, the amendments are effective for fiscal years and interim periods within those years beginning after December 15, 2011.&#160; For non-public companies, the amendments are effective for fiscal years and interim periods within those</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">55<a name="PB_55_152021_536"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">years ending after December 15, 2012.&#160; Early adoption is permitted because compliance with the amendments is already permitted.&#160; The amendments do not require transition disclosures.&#160; Riverview is currently assessing the impact that ASU 2011-05 will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December 2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-12, <i>Comprehensive Income (Topic 220): Deferral of the Effective Date for Amendments to the Presentation of Reclassifications of Items Out of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income in Accounting Standards Update No. 2011-05, </i>which defers certain provisions of ASU 2011-05,<i> Presentation of Comprehensive Income</i>.&#160; One of ASU 2011-05&#146;s provisions requires entities to present reclassification adjustments out of accumulated other comprehensive income by component in both the statement in which net income is presented and the statement in which other comprehensive income is presented (for both interim and annual financial statements).&#160; Accordingly, this requirement is indefinitely deferred by ASU 2011-12 and will be further deliberated by the FASB at a future date.&#160; ASUs 2011-05 and 2011-12 are effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December 15, 2011, and should be applied retrospectively for all periods presented in the financial statements.&#160; Riverview has not yet decided which statement format it will adopt.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September 2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-08, <i>Intangibles &#151; Goodwill and Other (Topic 350) &#151; Testing Goodwill for Impairment. </i>ASU 2011-08 allows companies to assess qualitative factors to determine if it is more-likely-than-not that goodwill might be impaired whether it is necessary to perform the two-step goodwill impairment test required under current accounting standards.&#160; This guidance is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2011, and early adoption is permitted.&#160; Riverview is currently evaluating this guidance, but does not expect the adoption will have a material effect on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">I</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">n December 2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-11, <i>Balance Sheet (Topic 210): Disclosures about Offsetting Assets and Liabilities</i>.&#160; The ASU requires new disclosures regarding the nature of an entity&#146;s rights of setoff and related arrangements associated with its financial instruments and derivative instruments.&#160; The new disclosures are designed to make GAAP financial statements more comparable to those prepared under International Financial Reporting Standards.&#160; The new disclosures entail presenting information about both gross and net exposures.&#160; The new disclosure requirements are effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2013, and interim periods therein; retrospective application is required.&#160; Riverview has not yet completed its evaluation of this ASU.&#160; However, since the provisions of ASU 2011-11 are disclosure-related, Riverview&#146;s adoption of this ASU is not expected to have an impact to its financial condition or results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 2 - Restriction on Cash and Due from Banks</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank is required to maintain average reserve balances in cash or on deposit with the Federal Reserve Bank.&#160; The required reserve at December 31, 2011and 2010 approximated $6,958,000 and $3,257,000, respectively.&#160; In addition, the Bank&#146;s other correspondents may require average compensating balances as part of their agreements to provide services.</font></p>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">credit quality or specific investment concerns warrant a sale of securities.&#160; Consideration is given to (1) the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, (2) the credit quality or financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer, and (3) the intent and ability of the Corporation to retain its investment in the issuer for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December 31, 2011, two CMO securities had unrealized losses as compared with nineteen securities at December 31, 2010, of which eighteen were municipal bonds and one was a mortgage-backed security.&#160; Management believes the unrealized losses relate to changes in interest rates since the individual securities were purchased as opposed to underlying credit issues.&#160; As management does not intend to sell any debt securities, and it is more likely than not that management will not be required to sell any debt securities before the cost bases are recovered, no declines are deemed to be other-than-temporary.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As part of its strategy to reduce some of the prepayment risk inherent within the investment portfolio, the Bank sold ten available-for-sale mortgage-backed securities during 2011 totaling $19,989,000 as compared with 2010 when it sold two available-for-sale securities totaling $6,350,000.&#160; On a year to date basis, gross realized gains for 2011 amounted to $274,000 and gross realized losses were zero, resulting in a $274,000 net gain from the sale.&#160; The Bank reinvested the proceeds from the sale by purchasing fixed rate mortgage-backed securities which not only provide interest income but also provide a more stable cash flow during future periods.&#160; Gross realized gains from the 2010 sale of investment securities amounted to $6,000, while there were no gross realized losses, resulting in a $6,000 net gain from the sale.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 4 &#151; Credit Quality for Loans and the Allowance for Loan Losses</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank monitors its loan portfolio on a regular basis with consideration given to detailed analysis of loans by portfolio segment.&#160; Portfolio segments represent pools of loans with similar risk characteristics.&#160; There are eight portfolio segments &#151; commercial loans; non-owner occupied commercial real estate loans; owner occupied commercial real estate loans; one-to-four family investment property loans; commercial land/land development/construction loans; residential real estate loans; home equity lines of credit; and consumer loans.&#160; For the purpose of estimating the allowance for loan losses, each of the segments for commercial loans, non-owner occupied commercial real estate loans, owner occupied commercial real estate loans, one-to-four family investment property loans, and commercial land/land development/construction loans have sub-segments for loan participations bought, and loans generated by Riverview&#146;s newly opened branch in Cressona and commercial office in Pottsville, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania.&#160; The loans in these sub-segments have risk characteristics that differ from the general segments and merit separate analysis in order to afford additional granularity and accuracy in management&#146;s estimate for the allowance for loan losses.&#160; Internal policy requires that the Chief Credit Officer report to the Board of Directors on a quarterly basis as to the status of the loan portfolio and any related credit quality issues.&#160; These reports include information on past due and nonaccrual loans, impaired loans, the allowance for loan losses and changes in the allowance for loan losses, credit quality indicators and foreclosed assets.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Past Due Loans and Nonaccrual Loans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans are considered to be past due when they are not paid in accordance with contractual terms.&#160; Past due loans are monitored by portfolio segment and by severity of delinquency &#151; 30-59 days past due; 60-89 days past due; and 90 days and greater past due.&#160; The accrual of interest is discontinued when the contractual payment of principal or interest has become 90 days past due or management has serious doubts about further collectability of principal or interest, even though the loan is currently performing.&#160; A loan may remain on accrual status if it can be documented that it is well secured and in the process of collection.&#160; When a loan is placed on nonaccrual status, all unpaid interest credited to income in the current calendar year is reversed and all unpaid interest accrued in prior calendar years is charged against the allowance for loan losses.&#160; Interest payments received on nonaccrual loans are either applied against principal or reported as interest income according to management&#146;s judgment as to the collectability of principal.&#160; Generally, loans are restored to accrual status when the obligation is brought current, has performed in accordance with contractual terms for a reasonable period of time and the ultimate collectability of the total contractual principal and interest is no longer in doubt.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The recorded investment in loans greater than 90 days and still accruing was $1,073,000 at December 31, 2011 as compared with $1,535,000 at December 31, 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Included within the loan portfolio are loans in which the Bank discontinued the accrual of interest due to the deterioration in the financial condition of the borrower.&#160; Such loans approximated $4,709,000 and $2,779,000 at December 31, 2011 and December 31, 2010, respectively.&#160; If the nonaccrual loans had performed in accordance with their original terms, interest income would have increased by $216,000 for the twelve months ended December 31, 2011 and $138,000 for the twelve months ended December 31, 2010, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following presents loans by loan portfolio segments that were on a nonaccrual status as of December 31, 2011 and December 31, 2010:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Impaired Loans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A loan is considered impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Bank will be unable to collect the scheduled payments of principal or interest when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&#160; Factors considered by management in determining impairment include payment status, collateral value, and the probability of collecting scheduled principal and interest payments when due.&#160; Loans that experience insignificant payment delays and payment shortfalls generally are not classified as impaired.&#160; Management determines the significance of payment delays and payment shortfalls on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration all of the circumstances surrounding the loan and the borrower, including the length of the delay, the reasons for the delay, the borrower&#146;s prior payment record, and the amount of the shortfall in relation to the principal and interest owed.&#160; The Bank further identifies all loans in nonaccrual status and troubled debt restructured loans as impaired loans, except large groups of smaller balance homogeneous loans that are collectively evaluated for impairment.&#160; Accordingly, the Bank does not separately identify individual consumer and residential loans for impairment disclosures, unless the loans are the subject of a restructuring agreement. Impairment is measured on a loan by loan basis for commercial and construction loans by either the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#146;s effective interest rate, or the loan&#146;s obtainable market price, or the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral dependent.&#160; When the measure of an impaired loan results in a realizable value that is less than the recorded investment in the loan, the difference is recorded as a specific valuation allowance against that loan and the Bank will make the appropriate adjustment to the allowance for loan losses.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following presents impaired loans by loan portfolio segments as of December 31, 2011 and December 31, 2010:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%" style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100.0%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The recorded investment in impaired loans increased by $4,156,000 at December 31, 2011 since December 31, 2010.&#160; This increase is attributable primarily to two unrelated commercial loan relationships that were identified as impaired in the latter part of the first quarter of 2011, one unrelated commercial loan relationship and two unrelated residential real estate loans that were identified as impaired in the second quarter of 2011, one unrelated commercial loan relationship that was identified as impaired in the third quarter of 2011, and one unrelated commercial loan relationship that was identified as impaired in the fourth quarter of 2011.&#160; Each of these loans was measured for impairment and additions were made to the allowance for loan losses based on the measurement and as deemed appropriate by management.</font></p>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Impaired loans also include all loans modified and identified as troubled debt restructurings (&#147;TDR&#148;).&#160; A loan is deemed to be a TDR when the Bank agrees to a modification in terms of a loan resulting in a concession made by the Bank in an effort to mitigate potential loss arising from a borrower&#146;s financial difficulty.&#160; As of December 31, 2011 there were eighteen restructured loans totaling $5,230,000 to seven separate and unrelated borrowers who were experiencing financial difficulty.&#160; The modifications on these loans included reductions in interest rates, extension of maturity dates and provisions for interest only payments.&#160; There is a commitment to extend additional funds in the amount of $300,000 to one of these borrowers for the completion of construction on an income generating property.&#160; Extension of these additional funds is necessary and prudent to ensure the continued economic viability of the project, which is the repayment source for the loan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table presents the number of loans and recorded investment in loans restructured and identified as troubled debt restructurings for the twelve months ended December 31, 2011, as well as the number and recorded investment in these loans that subsequently defaulted.&#160; Defaulted loans are those which are 30 days or more past due for payment under the modified terms.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of adopting the amendments in Accounting Standards Update No. 2011-2, <i>Receivables (Topic 310): A Creditor&#146;s Determination of Whether a Restructuring is a Troubled Debt Restructuring</i>, Riverview reassessed all restructurings that occurred on or after the beginning of the current fiscal year, effective January 1, 2011, for identification as a troubled debt restructurings.&#160; There were no restructurings that occurred on or after the beginning of the current fiscal year for which the allowance for loan losses had previously been measured under a general allowance for loan losses methodology.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Allowance for Loan Losses</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The allowance for loan losses is composed of individual valuation allowances to absorb probable and quantifiable losses based upon current knowledge of the loan portfolio, and loan pool valuation allowances, allocated and unallocated, to absorb losses which are not specifically identified but are inherent in the portfolio.&#160; Management evaluates the adequacy of the allowance on a quarterly basis.&#160; If the allowance for loan losses is not sufficient to cover actual loan losses, the Bank&#146;s earnings may be reduced.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Individual valuation allowances are established in connection with specific loan reviews and the asset classification process including the procedures for impairment testing.&#160; Such a valuation, which includes a review of loans for which full collectability in accordance with contractual terms is not reasonably assured, considers the estimated fair value of the underlying collateral less the costs to sell, if any, or the present value of expected future cash flows, or the loan&#146;s observable market value.&#160; Any shortfall that exists from this analysis results in a specific allowance for the loan.&#160; Pursuant to policy, loan losses must be charged off in the period the loans, or portions thereof, are deemed uncollectible.&#160; Assumptions and judgments by management in conjunction with outside sources are used to determine whether full collectability of a loan is not reasonably assured.&#160; These assumptions and judgments are also used to determine the estimates of the fair value of the underlying collateral or the present value of expected future cash flows or the loan&#146;s observable market value.&#160; Individual valuation allowances could differ materially as a result of changes in these assumptions and judgments.&#160; Individual loan analyses are performed quarterly on specific loans considered to be impaired.&#160; The results of the individual valuation allowances are aggregated and included in the overall allowance for loan losses.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loan pool valuation allowances represent loss allowances that have been established to recognize the inherent risks associated with the Bank&#146;s lending activity, but which, unlike individual allowances, have been allocated to unimpaired loans within the following eight portfolio segments: commercial loans; non-owner occupied commercial real estate loans; owner occupied commercial real estate loans; one-to-four family investment property loans; commercial land/land development/construction loans; residential real estate loans; home equity lines of credit; and consumer loans.&#160; Each of the segments for commercial loans, non-owner occupied commercial real estate loans, owner occupied commercial real estate loans, one-to-four family investment property loans, and commercial land/land development/ construction loans have sub-segments for loan participations bought, and for loans generated by Riverview&#146;s new branch office in Cressona, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania.&#160; The loans in these sub-segments have risk characteristics that differ from the general segments and merit separate analysis in order to afford additional granularity and accuracy in management&#146;s estimate for the allowance for loan losses.&#160; The Bank measures estimated credit losses on each of these groups of loans based on the historical loss rate of each group.&#160; The historical loss rate is calculated based on the average</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">65<a name="PB_65_152204_9862"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">annualized net charge-offs over the most recent eight calendar quarters.&#160; Unimpaired criticized and classified loans are further segregated as &#147;sub- pools&#148; within each of these eight segments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A separate, higher loss factor is ascribed to each of these &#147;sub-pools&#148; based on the relative risk in each segment as indicated by historical loss ratios, the level of criticized/classified assets, and the nature of each segment in terms of collateral and inherent risk of the loan type.&#160; Management believes that historical losses or even recent trends in losses do not form a sufficient basis to determine the appropriate level for the allowance.&#160; Management therefore also considers the following qualitative factors that are likely to cause estimated credit losses associated with each of the portfolio segments to differ from historical loss experience:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in lending policies and procedures, including changes in underwriting standards;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in national, regional and local economic and business conditions and developments that affect the collectability of the portfolio;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in the nature and volume of the portfolio and in the terms of loans;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in the experience, ability and depth of lending management and other relevant staff;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in the volume and severity of past due loans, the volume of non-accrual loans, and the volume and severity of adversely classified loans;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in the quality of the Bank&#146;s loan review system;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The existence and effect of any concentrations of credit, and the changes in the level of such concentrations; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The effect of other external factors such as competition and legal and regulatory requirements in the level of estimated credit losses in the existing portfolio.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each portfolio segment is examined quarterly with regard to the impact of each of these factors on the quality and risk profile of the pool, and adjustments ranging from zero to fifty basis points per factor are calculated.&#160; The sum of these qualitative factor adjustments are added to the historical loss ratio for each segment and the resulting percentage is applied to the loan balance of the segment to arrive at the required loan pool valuation allowance.&#160; An unallocated valuation allowance estimate is also made generally in order to give effect to significant loan growth in the fourth quarter of 2011 resulting from the opening of a new branch in Cressona and a commercial office in Pottsville, Schuylkill County Pennsylvania.&#160; This is a new market for the Bank and the portfolio has not yet developed any loss history.&#160; Growth is expected to continue in this portfolio, to be centered in business, construction, and commercial real estate loans.&#160; These loans are normally larger and more complex, and their collection rates are harder to predict.&#160; Management determines the unallocated portion, which represents the difference between the reported allowance for loan losses and the calculated allowance for loan losses, based generally on the following criteria:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">risk of imprecision in the specific and general reserve allocations;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">other potential exposure in the loan portfolio, including covering the risks in the growing book of loans in the Schuylkill County region;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">variances in management&#146;s assessment of national and local economic conditions; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">other internal or external factors that management believes appropriate at the time.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The loan pool valuation allowance for each segment along with the unallocated valuation</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">66<a name="PB_66_152204_9111"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>
<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='66',FILE='C:\JMS\C901053\11-32225-1\task5211853\32225-1-by.htm',USER='C901053',CD='Mar 24 23:25 2012' -->

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">allowance is summed and added to the individual valuation allowance for impaired loans to arrive at the total allowance for loan losses.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These evaluations are inherently subjective because even though they are based on objective data, it is management&#146;s interpretation of the data that determines the amount of the appropriate allowance.&#160; If the evaluations prove to be incorrect, the allowance for loan losses may not be sufficient to cover losses inherent in the loan portfolio resulting in additions to the allowance for loan losses and a reduction in Bank earnings.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Loan Charge Offs</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Charge offs of commercial and industrial loans and commercial real estate and construction loans are recorded promptly upon determination that all or a portion of any loan balance is uncollectible.&#160; A loan is considered uncollectible when the borrower is 90 days or more delinquent in principal or interest repayment and the following conditions exist:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is unlikely that the borrower will have the ability to pay the debt in a timely manner.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Collateral value is insufficient to cover the outstanding indebtedness.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Guarantors do not provide adequate support.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All unsecured consumer loans are charged-off when they become 120 days delinquent or when it is determined that the debt is uncollectible.&#160; Overdrafts are charged off when it is determined recovery is not likely or the overdraft becomes 45 days old, whichever comes first.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All secured consumer loans, except those secured by a primary or secondary residence, are charged off when they become 120 days delinquent, or when it is determined that the debt is uncollectible.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Uncollateralized portions of first mortgage residential real estate loans and consumer loans secured by real estate are charged off upon completion of a sheriff&#146;s sale, but prior to the transfer of the fair value carrying balance to other real estate owned.&#160; Current appraisals are obtained to determine the appropriate carrying balance with any exposed portion of the loan </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">principal balance being charged off.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">67<a name="PB_67_152204_2270"></a></font></p>
