<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loans (carried at cost):</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair values of loans are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses, using market rates at the balance sheet date that reflect the credit and interest rate-risk inherent in the loans.&#160; Projected future cash flows are calculated based upon contractual maturities or call dates, projected repayments and prepayments of principal.&#160; Generally, for variable rate loans that reprice frequently and with no significant change in credit risk, fair values are based on carrying values.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Impaired loans (generally carried at fair value):</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Impaired loans are those that are accounted for under the standard regarding <i>Accounting by Creditors for Impairment of a Loan, </i>in which the Corporation has measured impairment generally based on the fair value of the loan&#146;s collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is generally determined based upon independent third-party appraisals of the properties, or discounted cash flows based upon the expected proceeds.&nbsp;&nbsp;These assets are included as Level 3 fair values, based upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurements.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2011, the fair value consists of the loan balances of $1,666,000, net of a valuation allowance of $662,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Restricted investment in Bank stocks (carried at cost):</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount of restricted investment in Bank stock approximates fair value, and considers the limited marketability of such securities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Accrued interest receivable and payable (carried at cost):</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount of accrued interest receivable and accrued interest payable approximates its fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Deposit liabilities (carried at cost):</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair values disclosed for demand deposits (e.g., interest and noninterest checking, passbook savings and money market accounts) are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date (i.e., their carrying amounts).&#160; Fair values for fixed-rate certificates of deposit are estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that applies interest rates currently being offered in the market on certificates to a schedule of aggregated expected monthly maturities on time deposits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Short-term borrowings (carried at cost):</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amounts of short-term borrowings approximate their fair values.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Long-term borrowings (carried at cost):</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair values of FHLB advances are estimated using discounted cash flow analysis, based on quoted prices for new FHLB advances with similar credit risk characteristics, terms and remaining maturity.&#160; The prices were obtained from an active market and represent a fair value that is deemed to represent the transfer price if the liability were assumed by a third party.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Off-balance sheet financial instruments (disclosed at cost):</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair values for the Corporation&#146;s off-balance sheet financial instruments (lending commitments and letters of credit) are based on fees currently charged in the market to enter into similar agreements, taking into account, the remaining terms of the agreements and the counterparties&#146; credit standing.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 17 &#151; Subsequent Events</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Generally accepted accounting principles establish general standards for accounting for and disclosure of events that occur after the balance sheet date but before the financial statements are issued.&#160; In preparing these consolidated financial statements, Riverview evaluated the events and transactions that occurred from the date of the financial statements through the date these consolidated financial statements were issued, and has not identified any events that require recognition or disclosure in the consolidated financial statements except for updates discussed in Note 8 - Pension and Other Benefit Plans included in these financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM&nbsp;9A</font></u></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">. <u>CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</u>.</font></b><a name="Item9a_ControlsAndProcedures__123642"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Riverview&#146;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer (Principal Accounting Officer) carried out an evaluation of the effectiveness of the design and the operation of Riverview&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures (as such term is defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act) as of December&nbsp;31, 2011, pursuant to Exchange Act Rule&nbsp;15d-15.&#160; Based upon that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer along with the Chief Financial Officer (Principal Accounting Officer) concluded that Riverview&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures as of December&nbsp;31, 2011, are effective in timely alerting them to material information relating to Riverview that is required to be in Riverview&#146;s periodic filings under the Exchange Act.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Controls Over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There have been no changes in Riverview&#146;s internal control over financial reporting during the fourth quarter of 2011 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, Riverview&#146;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Riverview Financial Corporation Management&#146;s Report on Internal Controls Over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation is responsible for the preparation, integrity, and fair presentation of the financial statements included in this annual report.&#160; The financial statements and notes included in this annual report have been prepared in conformity with United States generally accepted accounting principles and include some amounts that are based on management&#146;s best estimates and judgments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management of the Corporation is responsible for establishing and maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting that is designed to produce reliable financial statements in conformity with United States generally accepted accounting principles.&#160; The system of internal control over financial reporting as it relates to the financial statements is evaluated for effectiveness by management and tested for reliability through a program of internal audits.&#160; Actions are taken to correct potential deficiencies as they are identified.&#160; Any system of internal control, no matter how well designed, has inherent limitations, including the possibility that a control can be circumvented or overridden and misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected.&#160; Also, because of changes in conditions, internal control effectiveness may vary over time.&#160; Accordingly, even an effective system of internal control will provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management assessed the Corporation&#146;s system of internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2011, in relation to criteria for effective internal control over financial reporting as described in &#147;Internal Control &#151; Integrated Framework&#148;, issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (&#147;COSO&#148;).&#160; Based on this assessment, management concludes that as of December&nbsp;31, 2011, its system of internal control</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">93<a name="PB_93_153831_9138"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Riverview maintains a &#147;Director Deferred Fee Agreement&#148; (DDFA) which allows electing directors to defer payment of their director fees until a future date.&#160; Under this agreement, the estimated present value of the future benefits is accrued over the effective dates of the agreement at an interest rate that is declared annually by the Board of Directors.&#160; Accordingly, the</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Board of Directors declared the interest rate to be 5.25% for 2011 for the Agreement with Director Garst and 8.00% for 2011 for the Agreements with Directors Alexander and Fox.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A Director Emeritus Agreement (the &#147;Agreement&#148;) effective November 2, 2011 was entered into by and between Riverview and its wholly owned subsidiary, Riverview Bank, and the directors.&#160; In order to promote the orderly succession of the board of directors, the Agreement defines the benefits the Bank is willing to provide upon the termination of service to those individuals who currently serve as directors of Riverview as of December 31, 2011, provided the director provides the services contemplated in the Agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Among various provisions, the material terms of the Agreement are as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank shall pay the director or the director&#146;s beneficiary $15,000 per year, which may be increased at the sole discretion of the board of directors, for five years and paid in 12 equal monthly installments in the following circumstances:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon termination of service as a director on or after the age of 65, provided the director agrees to provide certain ongoing services for the Bank;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon termination of service as a director due to a disability prior to the age of 65;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank shall not pay any benefits under the Agreement (1) to the extent limited by Section 280G of the Internal Revenue Code or which would be prohibited as a golden parachute payment, (2) the director is terminated for cause, as defined in the Agreement, (3) the director is removed by the Bank&#146;s regulator, (4) if the director engages in competition with the Bank after termination of service, or (5) if the director commits suicide within two years after the date of the Agreement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr. Zwally would receive one times his Annual Compensation as defined in the agreement, payable in a lump sum as well as a continuation of all non-cash benefits for one year if he would be terminated without cause.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If the payments are determined to be parachute payments and the executives are subject to excise taxes, they will receive an additional cash payment in an amount such that the after-tax proceeds of such payment will be equal to the amount of the excise tax.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January 24, 2012 Second Amended and Restated Executive Employment Agreements and Noncompetition Agreements were adopted by and between Riverview, the Bank and Messrs. Garst and Fox.&#160; The employment agreements were amended and restated to include recent guidance by the Internal Revenue Service regarding Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.&#160; The purpose for the noncompetition agreements was to define the restrictions placed on the executives during and after their employment with Riverview and the Bank in terms of being engaged in certain activities which may be considered to be competitive with the goodwill and proprietary rights of Riverview and the Bank.&#160; In consideration of the executives entering into this agreement, the Bank shall:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">pay the executives $10,250 upon the execution of the noncompetition agreement;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">provide the executives with a membership at a country club during their employment; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">provide the executives with an additional $10,000 in supplemental term insurance during their employment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Riverview maintains an &#147;Executive Deferred Compensation&#148; program in which one of Riverview&#146;s executives has signed an agreement.&#160; This agreement, which was initiated during 2010, allows executives of Riverview to defer payment of their base salary, bonus and performance based compensation until a future date.&#160; Under this agreement, the estimated present value of the future benefits is accrued over the effective dates of the agreement at an interest rate that is declared annually by the Board of Directors.&#160; Accordingly, the Board of Directors declared the interest rate to be 8.00% for 2011.&#160; The agreement is unfunded, with benefits to be paid from Riverview&#146;s general assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Elements of Executive Compensation</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:38.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Riverview&#146;s executive compensation and benefits package consists of direct compensation and corporate sponsored benefit plans, including base salary, bonuses, health and welfare benefits, profit sharing/401(k) plan, and stock option plans.&#160; Each component is designed to contribute to a total package that is competitive, performance-based, valued by the executives of the corporation and to align their interests with those of the shareholders.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Base salary</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A competitive base salary is necessary to attract and retain talented executives.&#160; The base salary for each named executive officer is determined based upon experience, expected personal performance, salary levels that are in place for comparable positions within the industry, and responsibilities assumed by the named executive officers.&#160; While an executive officer&#146;s initial salary is determined by an assessment of competitive market levels, the major factor in determining base salary increases is individual performance.&#160; The Compensation Committee evaluates executive officer base salary levels on an annual basis.&#160; Riverview usually grants annual increases to executives as well as increases needed to reflect changes in responsibilities and the market competitive environment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In establishing base salaries for 2011, the Compensation Committee considered the corporation&#146;s financial performance in comparison with historical trends and peer group and market based industry data.&#160; In consideration of the difficult economic conditions prevailing in 2011 and Riverview&#146;s financial performance in spite of such conditions, and to maintain a competitive salary base for the executive officers, the Committee determined that an increase in base salary for 2011 was appropriate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bonuses</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The annual bonus is tied to the corporation&#146;s performance and is not only granted to the named executive officers but is granted to all employees of the corporation.&#160; This award is made at the discretion of the Board of Director if the Board is of the opinion that such an award is merited.&#160; The bonus is designed to align the employees&#146; interests with those of shareholders by linking the corporation&#146;s performance to such a cash award.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:38.0pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Profit Sharing/401(k) Plan</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Executive officers participate in the Profit Sharing/401(k) Plan, which is offered to all full-time employees who have completed at least one year of service and are at least 18 years of age.&#160; This plan is a means for employees to contribute and save for their retirement, and it has a combined tax qualified savings feature and profit sharing feature for employees.&#160; Riverview makes a contributory match to the plan for each participating employee of 4% of their respective compensation.&#160; Riverview may also make a discretionary contribution annually to the plan based upon the corporation&#146;s financial performance.&#160; This discretionary contribution is designed to award employees for contributing to Riverview&#146;s financial success.&#160; Contributions are expressed as a percentage of base salary and executive officers receive the same percentage of base salary as all other employees.&#160; During 2011, the percentage of the discretionary contribution made to all eligible 401(k) participants was approximately 5%.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">102<a name="PB_102_153948_3536"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.3pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock Option Plan</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January 2009 Riverview implemented a nonqualified stock option plan as discussed below.&#160; The purpose of the 2009 Stock Option Plan was to advance the development, growth and financial condition of Riverview by providing incentives through participation in the appreciation of the common stock of Riverview to secure, retain and motivate Riverview&#146;s directors, officers and key employees and to align such person&#146;s interests with those of Riverview&#146;s shareholders.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.3pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2008, HNB Bancorp implemented a supplemental executive retirement plan covering Kirk D. Fox, who at the time was an Executive Vice President of HNB Bancorp.&#160; The plan was assumed by the Corporation after the consolidation of HNB Bancorp with First Perry Bancorp, forming Riverview Financial Corporation.&#160; Mr. Fox will receive $44,000 per year for 15 years beginning upon his termination of employment after age 65.&#160; Upon his termination of employment, he shall become fully vested in the benefit, unless his termination is due to cause as defined by the agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January 6, 2012, a supplemental executive retirement plan was adopted by and between the Bank and Brett D. Fulk, Chief Operating Officer of the Bank and was effective January 1, 2012.&#160; Mr. Fulk will receive $20,000 per year for 20 years beginning upon his termination of employment after reaching normal retirement age, unless his termination is due to cause as defined by the agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Perquisites</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Riverview provides an allowance for automobile use to Messrs. Garst, Fox and Fulk.&#160; In addition, they are entitled to a </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">membership at a country club during their employment.</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; These provisions are viewed as a normal and reasonable benefit in a highly competitive financial service industry.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 40.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">2009 Grants of Plan-Based Awards</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January 2009 the Corporation implemented a nonqualified stock option plan.&#160; The purpose of the 2009 Stock Option Plan was to advance the development, growth and financial condition of the Corporation by providing incentives through participation in the appreciation of the common stock of the Corporation to secure, retain and motivate the Corporation&#146;s directors, officers and key employees and to align such person&#146;s interests with those of the Corporation&#146;s shareholders.&#160; Effective January 4, 2012, shares of the Corporation&#146;s common stock that may be issued or transferred under this plan shall not exceed, in the aggregate, 220,000 shares at a purchase price of $10.60 per share.&#160; The vesting schedule is a seven year cliff, which means that the options are 100% vested in the seventh year following the grant date and the expiration date is ten years following the grant date.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January 2009, Riverview implemented a nonqualified stock option plan.&#160; The purpose of the 2009 Stock Option Plan was to advance the development, growth and financial condition of the Corporation by providing incentives through participation in the appreciation of the common stock of the Corporation to secure, retain and motivate the Corporation&#146;s directors, officers and key employees and to align such person&#146;s interests with those of the Corporation&#146;s shareholders.&#160; The following table discloses the number of outstanding options granted by Riverview to participants in equity compensation plans not approved by shareholders, as well as the number of securities remaining available for future issuance under the plans as of December 31, 2011.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM&nbsp;13</font></u></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">. <u>CERTAIN RELATIONSHIPS AND RELATED TRANSACTIONS, AND DIRECTOR INDEPENDENCE</u>.</font></b><a name="Item13_CertainRelationshipsAndRel_121737"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Currently, the Board of Directors has eleven (11) members.&#160; Under the Nasdaq Stock Market standards for independence, the following nine (9) directors meet the standards for independence:&#160; Messrs. Feld, Ford, Greenawalt, Hite, Hoover, Kerwin, Lebo, Schrantz and Troutman. This constitutes more than a majority of our Board of Directors.&#160; Only independent directors serve on our Audit Committee, Compensation Committee and Governance and Nominating Committee.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In determining the directors&#146; independence, the Board of Directors considered the services provided, loan transactions between Riverview Bank and the directors, their respective family members and businesses with whom they are associated, as well as any contributions made to non-profit organizations with whom the directors are associated.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Audit fees include professional services rendered for the audits of the consolidated financial statements of the corporation, quarterly review of the financial statements included in the corporation&#146;s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, consents and other assistance required to complete the year-end audit of the consolidated financial statements, including review of the corporation&#146;s Annual Report on Form 10-K, and review and consents of documents filed with the SEC, including out-of-pocket expenses.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Audit-related fees include reviews, analysis and consultations in regard to certain accounting transactions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Tax fees include fees billed for professional services rendered for tax compliance, tax advice and tax planning.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All other fees include fees billed for products and services provided that are other than the services reported under the Audit fees, Audit-related and Tax fees sections of the table above.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The report issued by Smith Elliott Kearns &amp; Company, LLC in connection with the audit of the financial statements of the corporation for the year ended December 31, 2011 did not contain an adverse opinion or a disclaimer of opinion, nor was such report qualified or modified as to uncertainty, audit scope, or accounting principles.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Audit Committee pre-approved all audit and permissible non-audit services provided by the independent auditors.&#160; These services may include audit services, audit related services, tax services and other services.&#160; The Audit Committee pre-approval process is generally provided for up to one year and any pre-approval is detailed as to the particular service or category of services and is subject to a specific budget.&#160; In addition, the Audit Committee may also pre-approve particular services on a case by case basis.&#160; For each proposed service, the independent auditor is required to provide detailed back-up documentation at the time of approval.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
